$comment: What .github/scripts/release-notes.py needs to know that is true of this repo
and no other. The rules it applies - which label means which section, that an
unlabelled pull request never reaches Features - are the same across the suite
and live in the script. The paths below are Konnekt's own: Kommands has no
website/ or agent_docs/, and a shared list would be wrong for both.
sets additionalProperties:false and its CI validates this repo's manifest
nightly, so a new key there is a change that has to land in kollektiv first.
This file has one consumer sitting next to it and needs no such coordination.
$nonAppPaths: Prefixes, matched against each changed file. A pull request touching only
these did not change the binary being downloaded, so it is left out of the
notes and counted in the footer instead.
website/ ships to Cloudflare Pages on its own. docs/ and agent_docs/ are read
in the repo. .github/ is CI and release tooling - the four pull requests that
built this very script described themselves to users as app changes before it
was listed here. .claude/ is agent configuration, scripts/ is repo tooling
(link check, coverage floor), and the root files are repo furniture; README.md
alone is what kept a website-only redesign in the notes. CONTRIBUTING.md and
SECURITY.md are the same class of furniture and were missing from this list
until the pull request that rewrote the type: label rules found it by being
filed as an app change itself.
Not listed, on purpose: build/ holds the app icon, .desktop file and RPM spec,
which do ship. frontend/ build config (eslint, vite, package.json) does not
ship either, but excluding it by path would also hide real frontend work in
the same pull request - that case is what the type:chore label is for.
